pr_title: Add key GoBack for close Settings
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**
Use key GoBack for close settings
Closes #4678
pr_comments: This pull request is no longer relevant with #5077.

issue_context.title: Escape key to exit settings
issue_context.body: I often try to exit the settings page using the escape key, as is convention in many other apps, such as discord and steam. I suggest the implementation of this feature, as I don't see any other use for the escape key in this situation.
comments:
It's a good idea.
I am always confused because the button to close is not in the same place as to open it. We could put a Close button at the bottom of the sidebar.

If the community accepts these changes, I can implement it.
I'm not sure about that last idea. Back buttons are typically on the top, usually to the left.
@voiiden Another option is to use the back button, it doesn't make much of a difference to me though.
Escape seems the most logical to me. It's literally called escape, as in escape from a menu, and backspace to go back is getting dated, usually getting replaced by Alt + Left arrow.
The reason I suggested back is because you are going back to the last page, esc is usually used for a dialog.
Settings page is full screen and not a modal. Esc is used for modal and transient surfaces, not for page navigation
@Jaiganeshkumaran Agreed, that's why I think we should use the back button.
This issue should be resolved with #5077.

review_comments: Can this be handled in the GoBack method?
Better yet, can we just declare the keyboard accelerator in the xaml so we don't have to register the event from code behind?

I tried this method first. There is a problem, especially visible on the widgets page .
The selection remains in keyboard mode and selects a block.
I tried to move the KeyboardAccelerator tag, use handle, nothing works.
Microsoft recommends this method to add a GoBack shortcut ([link](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/uwp/design/basics/navigation-history-and-backwards-navigation#support-access-keys)).

![Settings](https://i.ibb.co/LC5jSJj/settings.png)
The selection rectangle is the correct behavior when you navigate using the keyboard. In fact, this another reason to implement it this way.
You are right. I do it.
@yaichenbaum This method generates an error with GoBack. It compiles, but at runtime the enum cannot be parsed. I do not know why. However, it works for the other keys.
@yaichenbaum Using KeyboardAccelerator and Goback key is not possible. Maybe after pr #4858. This point is pending.
@cinqmilleans That PR will only upgrade the FullTrustProcess not the application itself.
@duke7553 The bug seem be in the framework. Change the .net version could fix it.
@cinqmilleans UWP doesn't have official support for .NET 5, the open PR only changes the framework for the FullTrustProcess.

@yaichenbaum This is the event that is currently used to detect button presses. My problem is detecting GoBack key. This cannot work with KeyboardAccelerator, but works for other keys. The method with CoreDispatcher works. I still say there is a bug with VirtualKey.GoBack in uwp.

@yaichenbaum I do not understand the question. I should not detect this event but trigger it. My problem is with VirtualKey.GoBack, which causes an error that other keys do not, although VirtualKey.GoBack exists in the enum, in the documentation, and intellisense. The event BackRequested works.
